## About this page

Vaults that live inside this one: nested vaults to keep things apart, and shared vaults that you and other people can open.

#### How it works

A nested vault is its own encrypted file, opened from inside this one without asking again.

A shared vault is held at a place you and the others can all reach, such as a shared folder or a WebDAV server. Each person has their own key to it, and the owner decides who is in. No server is needed.

Under **Yours**, each one says what it is: nested, shared with you, shared and yours to manage, or waiting for the owner's invitation. Click one to open it. **You are inside**, at the top, takes you back out.

#### When to use it

A nested vault for groups of items you want apart, such as work and home. A shared vault for a family or a small team.

#### Limits

What Settings, Security changes about a vault file, such as its passwords and duress passwords, applies only to the vault you opened at the door.

See also [Vaults inside a vault](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-vaults), [A nested vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-nested-vault), [A shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-shared-vault).

<a id="action-nested-vault"></a>

## A nested vault

Makes a separate vault in its own encrypted file, opened from inside this one.

#### How it works

Give it a name and its own password. From then on it opens from here without asking, because this vault holds its key. Its own password is for a recovery, or for opening the file somewhere else later.

#### Limits

It keeps things apart; it does not add protection. Anyone who can open this vault can open it too.

See also [Nested and shared vaults](/guide/settings/vaults/), [A shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-shared-vault).

<a id="action-shared-vault"></a>

## A shared vault

Makes a vault for a family or a team, kept at a place everyone can reach, without a server.

#### How it works

Give it a name, add your own name as the others will see it, and pick the place where it lives. WM Pass writes two files there: the vault, and the list of who holds its key, signed by you. The signature means the place cannot add anyone or swap someone's key.

People ask to join with [Join someone’s shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-join-shared-vault), and you add them under [People](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-vault-people).

When anyone saves, WM Pass merges with the copy at the place first, so changes from the others are not lost.

#### Limits

Everyone with the key can read and change everything in it.

Removing someone moves the vault to a new key, but they keep any copy they already have. Change the passwords they could see.

Everyone needs access to the place. A place that needs the network needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed) on each device.

See also [People](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-vault-people), [Join someone’s shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-join-shared-vault), [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place), [Vaults inside a vault](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-vaults).

<a id="action-join-shared-vault"></a>

## Join someone’s shared vault

Makes a code to send to the owner of a shared vault, so they can add you.

#### How it works

Type your name as the others will see it and choose **Make my code**. Show or send the code to the owner. It holds no secret.

Read the line of characters under it out to the owner. They compare it with what their screen shows, which proves nobody swapped your code on the way.

The owner sends back an invitation. The vault appears under **Yours** as waiting for it: click it, pick the place where the vault lives, paste the invitation and choose **Accept**.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Join someone's shared vault.

Type your name as the others will see it and choose **Make my code**. Show or send the code to the owner. It holds no secret.

Read the line of characters under it out to the owner. They compare it with what their screen shows, which proves nobody swapped your code on the way.

The owner sends back an invitation. The vault appears under **Yours** as waiting for it: tap it, pick the place where the vault lives, then paste the invitation or choose **Scan it**, and choose **Accept**.

See also [A shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-shared-vault), [People](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-vault-people).

<a id="action-vault-people"></a>

## People

Shows who holds a shared vault's key. The owner can add and remove people here.

#### How it works

Each person shows with their name and a fingerprint of their key.

To add someone, paste the code they made to join and choose **Check it**. Ask them to read their code out. If it matches the one shown, choose **It matches**, then give them the invitation that appears. Anyone can see the invitation, but only that person can use it.

To remove someone, use the remove button beside their name.

#### Limits

If the code they read out differs, choose **Not them**. A different one means someone swapped it, and adding it would hand that person the vault.

Removing someone moves the vault to a new key, so they cannot open anything written from then on. They may have kept a copy, so change any password they could see.

See also [A shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-shared-vault), [Join someone’s shared vault](/guide/settings/vaults/#action-join-shared-vault).
